hypothesis: If the claim holds, most species will have germ-cell (haploid) chromosome numbers between 6 and 16, with few species below 6 and fewer above 16.
pass_criterion: At least 70% of species with recorded haploid number n have 6 <= n <= 16, and the fraction with n > 16 is smaller than the fraction with n < 6.
fail_criterion: Fewer than 50% of species fall in 6-16, or the fraction with n > 16 exceeds the fraction with n < 6.
interpretation: 'Chromosomes in the germ-nuclei' means the reduced (haploid, n) number. Species-level counts in the Chromosome Counts Database, which covers plants only, are used, so the result applies to plants. Polyploid species are kept, since they are part of the real distribution.

dataset.name: Chromosome Counts Database (CCDB)
dataset.publisher: Tel Aviv University / Rice et al.
dataset.why_it_fits: Fields used: species name, gametic number (n), sporophytic number (2n) and reference, allowing the distribution of n to be computed.
